title: The Inhabited World and the Joy of Creation
english: Confessing and receiving beauty, having God within himself as a temple and becoming a sanctification, it is fitting that holiness and magnificence are said of such a thing; indeed, partaking in the holiness of the present God and Christ, the sanctification of God, and also of the Holy Spirit, and seeking that which is becoming and appropriate in great and superior things; for magnificence is that which is becoming in great things, but smallness is that which is in small things.

For you, indeed, if you wish to be well-appearing in human honors and dignities and in perceptible strength and wealth, you are small if you are in the sanctification of God through the one who has enriched according to those things assigned in the intelligible and spiritual virtues and piety, but he who seeks to excel in all great things and by this possesses magnificence, is a companion not unequal to the holiness which he has acquired (Ps 95:7-8).

Since we are servants of Christ, having his name called upon us, let us perform all things wisely and rationally, justly and holily, and let us bring glory to the name of Christ which is upon us. And also let the appearance of sacrifices be excellent; that is, elevate the concept concerning sacrifices, not plunging down low and slaughtering animals, but thinking highly of those things signified by them, the spiritual and heavenly sacrifices, of which the perceptible sacrifices are types and shadows (Ps 95:9b-11a).

And every intellect having possessed a worldly quality, shaken by sympathy toward matter, casts off the former and earthly disposition in order to take up the spiritual and heavenly nature. For truly, this is to have the earth shaken in order to pass into heaven and to put on the image of the heavenly.

Following this are the things brought about: 'The Lord has reigned among the nations' (Ps 97:1). For having suffered and having risen from the dead, He reigned among the nations, having said, 'All authority was given to me in heaven and on earth' (Mt 28:18). As it becomes the will of God as in heaven and on earth, and the Lord reigning in all the nations, the whole earth is shaken in the said manner from His face, so that the nature of virtue, having been made steadfast by the Lord, might take up the inhabited world instead of the earth, having become [steadfast], reigning...

For the Lord's [domain] is not merely earth but an inhabited world, with Father and Son and Holy Spirit dwelling in it and through divine gifts. He who ruled over all living things will judge the peoples with uprightness, judging according to his own order, since his wonders were announced to all, not only to Israel. He will judge them in uprightness, examining not only their works but also their dispositions. These things will happen according to his second coming, when the heavens will rejoice and the earth will exult (Ps 95:11-12a).

For the purpose of ascent, those bearing the image of the heavenly [one] and having citizenship in the heavens are heavens themselves, rejoicing in being laden with [fruit] coming from the Unconquerable from the true vine; wisdom poured it into the vessel. Some of these heavens are to inherit the high and above-lying earth through meekness, being called earth by a homonymous metonymy, rejoicing in the joy produced by the Holy Spirit.

If any mind is awakened by passions, as if by saltiness and bitterness, and the soul is treating the sea as a storm-tossed sea due to disordered movements, it is fitting for this to be shaken by a blessing, so that it might change from tossing and waves into stability and calm, according to its fullness, from the bitter and disordered. For the first blessing is for those who repent, to die to disordered and disturbed impulses. And those souls, because they have received the seed of Jesus, rejoice in unspeakable and glorified joy as they reap a harvest in tears amidst the exultation (Ps 95:12b-13b).

The 'then' refers to the inhabited world being made upright by the Lord. The 'then' also refers to 'Let the heavens rejoice.' For the heavens shall rejoice and the earth shall exult; then the trees of the forest shall exult (Ps 95:12b). The 'trees of the forest' are those not bearing fruit; but rather the former fruits bearing fruit exult, running ahead as the Lord comes down, 'Come!' For the Lord is coming to judge the earth, then the trees of the forest exult, always rejoicing like the trees of paradise in luxury. But of these not...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Cloud and Darkness of God's Incomprehensibility
english: For they are indeed woods of a grove, but unless the Lord shines upon them to bear edible fruit and to make [one] like an apple, as he says, in the midst of the brothers among the limbs: 'Like an apple in the trees of the grove, so is my brother among the sons' (Ps 95:12). For he himself from the beginning was bearing fruit in virtue, not knowing nor doing sin; therefore he also shares his own fruit-bearing quality with those who accompany the woods of the grove, being one who happens to be an apple in the midst.

He has established the inhabited world so that it shall no longer be shaken, in righteousness the coming Lord will judge (Ps 95:13c). And he will judge in truth, and the peoples, in whom his wonders have become manifest, just as the inhabited world receives a reward of holiness according to the righteousness by which it is judged, so the peoples shall receive a perfect knowledge, so that they might no longer know by parts but might face the truth personally and fully, receiving and contemplating it.

By the sufficient hand (but the spiritual David is not he who was born of his seed according to the flesh) the earth is established, all war-like noise and disturbance having been destroyed by him (Ps 96:1); the earth is established, taking up a stability according to how it received seed to bear fruit, in R and X and L, having sown for themselves into righteousness, so that the offspring of righteousness might multiply of those sown by Jesus. Therefore also the Lord reigns, not from not reigning at all, but having come to reign from the fact that those sinning have repented and turned toward the kingdom. All the earth rejoices, doing this, being protected in the fact that the Lord has reigned over all of it.

And regarding the rejoicing, the assigned land and islands shall be glad, that is, the men and the churches dwelling in them. And it is possible also to call the souls of the steadfast according to virtue 'islands,' being tossed about by the storm and the surge of the passions, yet suffering nothing of the whole from them. Into all the minds that are set forth, he will take that which is said by God: 'Draw near to me, islands.' For the set-forth islands, having been renewed by the teaching of the new covenant, will receive the word concerning the powers of God, which those who make the paradoxes of God are able to proclaim sufficiently, which he says the Spirit...
They proclaim his virtues (that is, the virtues of God) in the islands. And because all these things exist, it happens that the islands are being completely rejoiced (Ps 96:2-3).

A cloud and thick darkness are around him—not bodily; for if the circling things were bodies, and the one being circled were a body or using a body; but incorporeal, rather exceeding bodies, are God and his only-begotten Son as God the Word is. And he says now, to present his incomprehensibility around him, 'there is a cloud and thick darkness'; and perhaps the cloud signifies the words flowing from him, and the thick darkness the obscurity of his incomprehensibility. For it is said also previously, 'He inclines the heavens and comes down' (Ps 18:1), and 'thick darkness is under his feet' (Ps 97:5); for that which is hard to see, rather incomprehensible to the mind of created beings, is presented through the thick darkness under his feet as he travels creatively and providentially.

If it is possible to take these things well concerning the Savior according to the incarnation, examine whether it can be said that there is a cloud around him, the assumed human nature being indivisible in its modes, fulfilling the prophecy saying, 'Behold, the Lord sits upon a cloud of mist' (Isa 40:4) and he goes into Egypt. For he came into the so-called allegorically Egypt, the inhabited world, and, if it is said so, sitting kingly upon a cloud of mist, he by no means has the weight of sin; for he did not commit sin by watering the whole world through this cloud. But since the descent of the Lord into the aforementioned cloud is much hard to see, it is fitting that a thick darkness also coincides with the cloud around him.

'Righteousness and judgment are the strength of his throne; fire goes before him and blazes around his enemies' (Ps 97:3-5). The strength of the throne of his kingdom is righteousness and judgment, since he, as king, is a righteous judge. This is agreed with what is found in Proverbs: 'By righteousness a throne is prepared' (Prov 16:12). Therefore, since he is found to be a righteous judge, fire going before him blazes at all his enemies. title: The Righteousness of the Truth-Witnesses
english: Those who profess false doctrine and lie are enemies of the truth; and the friendship of the world makes one an enemy to God, as it is said. If one does not wish to be a friend of the world, he is established as an enemy of God, those being shown as enemies of God who embrace the worldly and more cosmic intercourse. These enemies are not consumed by the fire going before the Lord, which does not consume or corrupt their essence (for the subsistence of their soul is immortal), but it annihilates the works of the flesh and the material thoughts surrounding them; therefore the Savior prays that the fire which he came to cast upon the earth might be kindled, so that all earthly things might be consumed. This fire should not be considered the same as that which consumes burning substances, but it is of a different nature, differing greatly from the flame among us.

The bright words of his divine teaching flashed like lightning throughout the whole inhabited world (Ps 96:4), illuminating and lighting it with the light of knowledge, but the earth, seeing these lightnings, being shaken, changed, casting off its earthly quality in order to take up the image of the heavenly. And in another way: the earth was shaken seeing the laws of God resembling lightnings, as if human laws were to be transferred and the appropriate things were to be set for them. Not all men, having abandoned their own ancestral customs, have come to the evangelical instruction, but while the inhabited world sees the lightnings of the Lord, it is illuminated, yet the earth is shaken, receiving the beginning of the impulse to enrich the inhabited world itself, so that the divine lightnings of the Lord might appear to it having become such. And the rest similarly.

Those who preannounce the presence of the Savior here, who is the righteousness of God, are heavens (Ps 96:6), bearing the image of the heavenly and having citizenship in heaven, having announced the righteousness of God being released from heaven. When these things were brought to an end, the people followed to behold the glory of the Lord, which was not other than his righteousness. But since practical virtue is often called righteousness, only those who are righteous men can announce this practically, being heavens.
The righteous one proclaims faith, their faith being reckoned toward righteousness. And all the peoples, having become imitators of them, see the glory following this righteousness of God.

And likewise Zion will be thought of as entirely contemplative and theoretical regarding the truth, and the daughters of Judah, the souls confessing and praising God with thanksgiving for the wonderful things done through them. For Judah is interpreted as confession. And it is possible also to call all those things placed together with the Divine Scripture 'daughters of Judah'. Regarding 'Hear and be glad, O Zion' (Ps 95:2), such things are to be said: he who hears the divine words with understanding is always gladdened, seeing the beauties of the theorems made manifest by the teaching. Since Zion has been gladdened by having heard thus, the lesser daughters of Judah, being called to the judgments of God, will experience divine rejoicing according to how they will be judged, their minds being reasonably uplifted by the presence of the Holy Spirit.

If ever someone, intending harm to a holy person even unto bodily injury or death, strengthened the attacks, while the blameless and irreproachable soul remained, who would not confess the witnesses of the truth being guarded according to the souls by the Lord confessed by them? And if ever it should happen through inattention or slight oversight for the soul of a holy person to fall into the hand of a sinful devil or one of his kind, and the Lord rescues this one as having been set free from sins, the hands of the sinner are said to become under the hand of God. And concerning his holy disciples, he says to the Father, 'Father, keep them' (Jn 17:11); the same thing as 'to keep' is 'to guard'.

To the one who has perfected practical virtue, a light of knowledge has risen, called righteousness, which is nothing other than the light of the True One, concerning whom the Father is (Jn 1:1). To those who fear my name, the sun of righteousness rises (Ps 96:12). And when this light has shone upon the righteous, the heart has become straight; and God has caused gladness to rise to him having a straight heart, and for those partaking of the knowledge of the truth, having straight hearts, the righteous...
